- [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)

Fixes #196

- `README.md`: reworded the paragraph under "Try your first design". It previously implied unprefixed commands (e.g. `/egm-brainstorm`) work in Antigravity and only Claude Code needs the `/egm:` prefix. Antigravity (agy CLI) now also uses the `/egm:` prefix, e.g. `/egm:egm-brainstorm`. The example code blocks are unchanged.
- <other docs, e.g. `docs/getting_started.md`, `docs/harnesses.md`: same wording fix. Delete this line if none>

**Why:** per #196, in agy CLI 1.4.8 the unprefixed commands are not recognized; skills only load with the plugin namespace. Since the skills set `disable-model-invocation: true`, they don't appear in the model's skill list either, so the missing prefix is hard to discover.

**Scope:** docs only. Verified against the agy CLI; the Antigravity desktop app was not tested.

title: feat(site): add domain-gated GA4 and Cookie Notification Bar for egm.dev
body:
## Contribution Type

Please select the track that matches this pull request:

- [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

## Summary of Key Changes

List all key changes made in this pull request and why:

- **`site/src/layouts/Base.astro`**: Adds Google Cookie Notification Bar (`cookienotificationbar.min.{css,js}`, category `2A`, `siteId: 'egm.dev'`) with Consent Mode v2 default `denied` (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`, `wait_for_update: 500`) and Google Analytics 4 (`gtag.js`) with client-side URL/referrer filtering (`utm_*`/`gclid`/`dclid`/`gclsrc` allowlist, referrer origin+pathname only, `allow_google_signals: false`, `allow_ad_personalization_signals: false`). Double-gated on build-time `import.meta.env.PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID` and runtime `window.location.hostname === 'egm.dev'` so external forks, preview URLs, and local builds make zero requests to Google servers.
- **`site/src/components/Footer.astro`**: Adds the `Cookies management controls` button (`glue-cookie-notification-bar-control`), hidden by default via `aria-hidden="true"` and revealed automatically by the Cookie Notification Bar in eligible regions.
- **`.github/workflows/deploy-site.yml`, `site/README.md`, `site/astro.config.mjs`**: Passes `PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID: ${{ vars.PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID }}` during the GitHub Pages build and documents the `egm.dev`-only cookie and analytics scope.

- **Consent initialization**: Register the cookie-bar configured `loaded` callback before loading its script. Queue GA configuration and load its script exactly once after initial consent commands exist. If the callback never arrives, GA stays unloaded.
- **Regression coverage**: Add six Node tests and six built-page browser scenarios with intercepted Google responses. They cover delayed configuration, script failure, duplicate callbacks, noncanonical domains, an unset measurement ID and filtered page URLs. The original implementation fails the ordering regression.
- **PR CI**: Add a read-only Node 22 site-validation job using existing pinned actions: clean install, tests, Astro check, builds without analytics and with `G-TEST`, and browser checks. It does not deploy.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

- [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Verification

- [ ] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Executed `/egm-review docs/designs/<name>.md`, resolved findings via `/egm-resolve`, and verified relative links (`pytest tests/unit/test_link_integrity.py`).
- [x] **For Bug Fix / Implementation PRs (Stage 2)**: Unit tests or `test_scenarios.yaml` added/updated and `pytest tests/unit` executed (local Node 22: six Node tests and six browser scenarios passed; Astro check: 0 diagnostics; production builds passed with ID unset and `G-TEST`; 135 Python unit tests passed).
- [ ] **For Harness Support PRs**: Verified plugin installation and end-to-end execution of `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` on the target harness; attached execution summary or transcript.

## Verification limits and activation

Browser verification uses the built page and controlled intercepted Google responses. It verifies integration ordering, not the live Google consent service or GA collection. `PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID` remains unset, so analytics stays inactive. Supply the GA4 web-stream measurement ID separately before activation. Existing squash auto-merge and required reviews/checks remain in place.

title: README: Antigravity (agy CLI) also requires the /egm: prefix for skills
body:
README.md line 52 says: "Use the commands below in Antigravity. In Claude Code, use the `/egm:` prefix", and the examples show `/egm-brainstorm`.

In our testing with the agy CLI 1.4.8 (plugin installed via `agy plugin install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model`, EGM 0.1.0), the unprefixed commands such as `/egm-brainstorm` are not recognized. The skills only load when invoked with the plugin namespace, e.g. `/egm:egm-brainstorm` and `/egm:egm-drift-report`, both of which worked as expected.

Because the skills set `disable-model-invocation: true`, they also do not appear in the model's skill list, which makes the missing prefix harder to discover.

Suggested fix: update the README (and any matching docs) to say Antigravity also uses the `/egm:` prefix, e.g. `/egm:egm-brainstorm`.

Note: tested only with the agy CLI; we did not test the Antigravity desktop app.

title: fix(packaging): report missing OpenAI interface icons as ValueError
body:
## Contribution Type

Please select the track that matches this pull request:

- [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

## Summary of Key Changes

`build()` in `scripts/pack_plugin.py` read the OpenAI `composerIcon` and `logo` paths with `interface[key]`, so a manifest missing either key crashed with a bare `KeyError` instead of the descriptive `ValueError` the function's other validation checks raise.

To reproduce: remove `logo` from `extensions.com.openai.interface` in `plugin.json`, then run `python scripts/pack_plugin.py --target openai --output /tmp/out`. You get `KeyError: 'logo'`.

Fix: each key is now checked with `.get()`, and a missing or empty value raises `ValueError: Missing OpenAI interface reference: <key>`. Present values still flow through the existing "Unbundled manifest reference" check unchanged.

Behavior is otherwise unchanged: the interface still falls back to `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` only when `plugin.json` has no interface at all, so a single missing key is reported rather than looked up there.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

- [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Verification

- [ ] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Executed `/egm-review docs/designs/<name>.md`, resolved findings via `/egm-resolve`, and verified relative links (`pytest tests/unit/test_link_integrity.py`).
- [x] **For Bug Fix / Implementation PRs (Stage 2)**: Unit tests or `test_scenarios.yaml` added/updated and `pytest tests/unit` executed.
- [ ] **For Harness Support PRs**: Verified plugin installation and end-to-end execution of `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` on the target harness; attached execution summary or transcript.

Added `test_rejects_missing_openai_interface_icons` (parametrized over `composerIcon` and `logo`). It fails on `main` with `KeyError` and passes with this fix. `pytest tests/unit`: 137 passed.

title: [Feature]: Policy and scope for Turkish documentation localization
body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation
I want to contribute Turkish translations for EGM's documentation to help Turkish developers adopt the framework.

Before spending time on translations, I want to check your team's policy on localized docs. Because the English documentation will continue to evolve, in-tree translations can easily drift without an agreed review and maintenance approach.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview
Add Turkish translations for key documentation files (such as `README.md` and guides in `docs/`, likely under `docs/tr/`). Agent prompts and core plugin files will stay in English.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals
Goals:
* Translate core documentation (`README.md`, `docs/getting_started.md`, and design overviews).
* Keep industry terms and EGM concepts (Elephant, Goldfish, Spec, Harness, prompts) untranslated to avoid confusing terminology.
* Clarify whether you want in-tree community translations, or prefer documentation to stay English-only.

Non-Goals:
* Modifying system prompts in `skills/` or `agents/` (keeping prompts in English preserves reliable instruction following).
* Making code, config, or build changes.
* Opening a large translation PR without prior maintainer approval.

title: [Feature]: Add experimental jcode integration with native Swarm reviewers
body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

I would like to contribute jcode integration for EGM. jcode supports project-local skills and native Swarm workers, but EGM has no documented, verified installation path for this host. Copying only the skills is insufficient: reviewers also need canonical personas, document standards, reliable completion handling, and a clearly defined context boundary.

The proposed integration keeps packaging and workflow guidance in EGM. jcode already provides the necessary basic delegation primitives. Stronger per-worker memory or tool isolation would remain a jcode runtime capability, rather than a host-specific fork of EGM's reviewers.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Install the complete canonical runtime under a project's `.jcode/egm/`, with seven small entry points under `.jcode/skills/`. Refuse collisions, stage installation before publication, and remove only an unchanged installation identified by its file inventory. Do not modify global configuration or replace unrelated skills.

Map the root coordinator to Elephant and dispatch one fresh native worker for each Goldfish lens and review round. In jcode v0.99.1, only the root can spawn workers. `await_members` returns asynchronously, while `summary` contains abbreviated tool calls rather than complete findings. The integration must consume actual reports, preserve review-stage ordering, and close owned workers after retaining their findings.

Fresh workers do not imply memory isolation. A native diagnostic confirmed that a child could recall an intentionally stored project-memory value while remaining unaware of a parent-only marker; the diagnostic entry was subsequently forgotten. Closing a memory-enabled worker can also trigger final memory extraction. Process-scoped `JCODE_MEMORY_ENABLED=false` disables memory for both coordinator and workers, not just Goldfish. It does not provide filesystem isolation.

A local experimental candidate includes installation regression tests and opt-in native tests. The baseline is EGM `b3a35956759bf7f024af2ff061b2e0b44b438e4c` with jcode v0.99.1 (`7206efd0c`). Current evidence:

- 205 offline tests pass on Linux with Python 3.12 and under Wine with Windows Python 3.12. Wine is not native Windows CI.
- Six supplemental native tests pass: installed skill/resource loading and parent-history isolation; bootstrap/drift/resolution; configured default-memory isolation; the unapproved readiness gate; missing reviewer resources; and shared project-memory behavior.
- Full brainstorm → draft → ordered review completed with 15 fresh workers. Its original pytest reported a validator failure and cleanup error; after harness corrections, frozen native evidence passed all workflow checks without model re-execution. All 16 sessions are now Closed. This is not a fresh green end-to-end pytest run. Maintenance cleanup revalidation passed with the owned-server lifecycle; earlier failures remain recorded.
- Tests use a private `JCODE_RUNTIME_DIR` and owned temporary-server lifecycle. Separate sockets alone do not isolate reload state. This was a fixture configuration omission, not evidence of a jcode runtime bug. Session transcripts remain shared.

Before opening a design PR, I would appreciate maintainer alignment on whether jcode is in scope, whether this project-scoped installation surface is appropriate, and which shared host context is permissible for Goldfish reviews.

Relevant pinned source evidence:

- [Skill discovery and frontmatter](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/blob/7206efd0c/crates/jcode-base/src/skill.rs): project skill discovery; `disable-model-invocation` is not a parsed enforcement mechanism.
- [Swarm tool](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/blob/7206efd0c/crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/communicate.rs): native delegation and completion operations.
- [Worker lifecycle](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/blob/7206efd0c/crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/comm_session.rs) and [headless setup](https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/blob/7206efd0c/crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/headless.rs): fresh sessions, shared project memory, and shutdown behavior.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

**Goals**

- Reuse canonical EGM skills, personas and standards with correct installed resource paths.
- Document direct native dispatch, complete report retrieval, fresh reviewers per round, lifecycle cleanup and invocation-policy limitations.
- Preserve existing readiness gates, human decisions and review-stage ordering.
- Verify actual launch/read/completion traces; measure parent-history and shared-memory boundaries separately.
- Retain reproducible offline checks and opt-in model tests with explicit limitations.

**Non-Goals**

- Change EGM's review criteria or claim that prompts enforce read-only permissions.
- Change user-wide configuration, model selection or authentication.
- Maintain a jcode fork or depend on debug-only isolation.
- Claim native Windows model coverage, strict sandboxing, or supported-harness status from offline tests alone.

If accepted, I will follow the repository's contribution sequence: an issue approved for design, a reviewed Stage 1 design PR, then a Stage 2 implementation PR after design approval. No support claim or implementation PR is being published by this inquiry.

title: fix: hyphenate skill directories and drop $schema for omp (Oh My Pi) compatibility
body:
## Contribution Type

Please select the track that matches this pull request:

- [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

## Summary of Key Changes

List all key changes made in this pull request and why:

Fixes omp (Oh My Pi) skill discovery, in preparation for #186. omp v18.12.6 currently drops all seven EGM skills silently at plugin discovery, for two independently verified causes:

- **Skill directory names**: `skills/egm_brainstorm/` (underscore) declares `name: egm-brainstorm` (hyphen) in `SKILL.md` frontmatter. omp's skill validator only accepts directory names matching `[a-z0-9-]+`, so all seven skills are rejected at discovery. The seven directories are renamed to match the declared names (`git mv`; skill content unchanged except path references inside `TEST.md` / `test_scenarios.yaml`). Claude Code tolerates the mismatch, so this is invisible to the existing harnesses.
- **`$schema` in root `plugin.json`**: declaring `https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json` routes omp to its strict agent-plugins validator, which rejects the skills' `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter field. Bisected with probe plugins: under strict validation, `license` and folded (`>-`) descriptions pass; `disable-model-invocation` fails. The key is omitted so omp falls back to its permissive Claude-plugin scanner. `disable-model-invocation` is kept because user-only invocation is core to EGM's design; the strict rejection looks like an omp-side bug (that validator's closed field set excludes a field omp itself normalizes elsewhere).

Note on the Bug Fix guideline: the mechanical diff exceeds 100 lines because the directory renames touch path references across `README.md`, `docs/designs/*`, the Claude adapter, `pack_plugin.py`, tests, and the regenerated `distributions/claude/` tree. The substantive change is small: 7 renames + 1 removed JSON key.

title: [Feature]: Add support for OhMyPi (omp)
body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

Please add support for [Oh My Pi (OhMyPi / `omp`)](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi), an open-source coding-agent harness forked from Pi. It provides skills, extensions, and native subagents, making it a useful environment for EGM's Elephant/Goldfish workflow.

EGM currently documents other harnesses, but does not document an OhMyPi installation or delegation mapping. Users should be able to run EGM in OhMyPi without manually adapting installation paths, resource lookup, and reviewer dispatch.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Provide a documented, verified OhMyPi integration using its existing plugin/skill and subagent capabilities. Reuse EGM's shared skills, reviewer personas, and document standards rather than maintaining a separate copy of the workflow.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

**Goals**
- Document a supported installation path that makes the complete EGM package available, including `agents/` and `resources/document_standards/`, not just `skills/`.
- Document how users invoke EGM skills in OhMyPi and how reviewer personas map to its native `task` subagent tool.
- Preserve fresh-context Goldfish reviews without inheriting the Elephant's earlier conversation, with appropriate read-only reviewer access. Stop with a clear explanation when the required delegation capabilities are unavailable.
- Verify brainstorm → draft → review end to end in OhMyPi, including resource resolution, artifact output, and reviewer isolation; record the tested version and verification limits in the harness documentation/test record.

**Non-goals**
- Forking EGM's shared skill text or introducing a separate orchestration framework.
- Changing OhMyPi itself or adding support for unrelated harnesses.
- Claiming verified support based only on manifest validation or copied skill files.

## Related context

- #116 requests support for Hermes, OpenClaw, and Delta; this request is specifically for OhMyPi.
- [EGM harness support requirements](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/docs/harnesses.md#contributing-support-for-new-harnesses)
- [OhMyPi repository](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)

This is a feature inquiry for maintainer alignment, not an implementation or a claim that OhMyPi support has already been tested.

## Status review: 2026-10-27

PR #190 merged into main as `6040fc880211b63e7749045904641f414749c518`. Its skill-directory and manifest discovery fixes are present on current main `a8380ab5f0aba392c97e31c79f9a6666b3f09f14`. Its author reports skill resolution and persona registration on omp v18.12.6; brainstorm, draft, review, permission enforcement, and reviewer isolation are not established by that discovery result. The full host-verification and maintainer-approval requirements remain pending.

body:

## Summary of Key Changes

Since #136, Claude Code users approve Goldfish persona reads with Read rules, and `docs/claude.md` shows one example in the form `Read(//absolute/plugin/path/agents/**)`. Two things in that setup are easy to get wrong, and both fail silently: the rule simply never matches, and headless reviewers are denied their personas.

- **Windows path form.** Following the example with a Windows drive path gives `Read(//C:/Users/...)`, which Claude Code does not match. The forms that do match are `//c/Users/...` (lower-case drive letter, no colon) and a native `C:\Users\...\agents\**`. The docs now show both and name the one that does not work.
- **Version folders.** A marketplace install lives in `.../plugins/cache/<marketplace>/egm/<version>/`, so a rule naming one version stops matching after an update. Replacing only the version segment with `*` keeps matching across versions and still covers only this plugin's four resource folders. The docs now say so, with a four-line Windows example.

Changed: `docs/claude.md`, and `distributions/claude/docs/claude.md` regenerated with `scripts/pack_plugin.py`. No skill, persona or manifest changes.

This replaces my earlier #173, which fixed the read hook that #136 removed.

Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

v8.12.2

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

title: [Feature]: Add /ask-egm command for contextual help and guidance
body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation
Whenever a new skill or capability is released, demos and content creators make the workflow look flawless and intuitive, leaving users excited to try it. However, in reality, when users sit down to use the tool, they often experience "blank canvas syndrome"—freezing up and feeling completely lost on exactly what to type in the chatbox to achieve those same results.

Beyond this initial friction, users frequently need guidance on what to do next, which skills to load, or how to troubleshoot immediate problems while interacting with the agent. Currently, there is no dedicated, context-aware command to query the system for help regarding the current workflow state without muddying the main conversational thread. A built-in command would streamline the developer experience by providing immediate, context-aware assistance, bridging the gap between watching a perfect demo and actually executing a complex workflow.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)
Once maintainers apply status: approved-for-design, open a Stage-1 Design Doc PR adding docs/designs/ask-egm.md; when maintainers merge that PR, they will apply status: approved-for-pr for the Stage-2 Implementation PR.

### 1. Proposed Overview
Implement an /ask-egm slash command that allows users to ask the agent open-ended questions about their current context or anything. This command will act as an interactive help desk, enabling users to request the next logical steps, troubleshoot errors, and get recommendations on which specific skills to use for a given task.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals
#### In-Scope Goals:
- Create an /ask-egm <query> command for users to query the agent for contextual help.
- Analyze the current workflow state and suggest the next logical steps.
- Provide dynamic recommendations on which skills to load or utilize based on the user's intent.
- Troubleshoot immediate workflow problems or errors.

#### Out-of-Scope Non-Goals:
- Executing tasks, loading skills, or modifying files directly via the /ask-egm command (it acts strictly in an advisory capacity).
- Replacing standard prompt inputs for regular task generation.

title: fix(claude): approve plugin reads on Windows paths
body:
## Contribution Type

Please select the track that matches this pull request:

- [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

## Summary of Key Changes

On Windows, `allow_plugin_reads.sh` (added in #113) never approves a read, so Goldfish persona and standard reads fall back to permission prompts. Background subagents and headless runs cannot answer those prompts.

Cause: Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` with backslashes (`C:\Users\...\egm\0.1.0`, the same form as `installPath` in `installed_plugins.json`). `tool_input` arrives as JSON, so each backslash in the path is the two characters `\\`. The extraction group `([^"\\]*)` stops at the first backslash, so no Windows path ever matches.

Changes, all in `.claude-plugin/hooks/allow_plugin_reads.sh`:

- Decide the path style from `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` alone: a drive path (`C:\` or `C:/`) is Windows, anything else is POSIX.
- Windows roots: turn the root's backslashes into `/`, extract `file_path`/`path` with `(([^"\\]|\\\\)*)` (plain characters or escaped backslash pairs), turn each `\\` pair into `/`, and compare root and path in lower case, since Windows paths are case-insensitive.
- POSIX roots: path matching is unchanged from `main`. A backslash is a filename character there, so the original extraction still rejects any path that contains one, and the hook falls through to the normal permission rules. This addresses the review: the first revision normalised backslashes on every root, which let a root-level POSIX file named `agents\style.md` match `agents/`.
- On every root, treat Glob patterns starting with a drive letter (`C:`) or a backslash (`\\server\share`) as absolute, like `/` and `~`.

Any other escape (`\"`, `\uXXXX`) still extracts nothing, and the `..` guard still runs first on the raw input. UNC plugin roots are not treated as Windows paths, so they keep the normal prompt. No new tools are used (POSIX `sh`, `tr`, `sed -E`, `grep -E`).

#172 (now merged) made the existing hook tests run on Windows; this PR fixes the hook's behaviour for real backslash paths. If #136 removes the hook, that removal should take precedence over this change.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

## Verification

- [ ] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Executed `/egm-review docs/designs/<name>.md`, resolved findings via `/egm-resolve`, and verified relative links (`pytest tests/unit/test_link_integrity.py`).

- [ ] **For Harness Support PRs**: Verified plugin installation and end-to-end execution of `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` on the target harness; attached execution summary or transcript.

`tests/unit/test_harnesses.py` adds two parametrized tests that run the hook through `sh`:

- `test_claude_read_hook_handles_windows_paths` (13 cases): a backslash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` with JSON-escaped Windows paths, including drive, UNC, `..` and escaped-quote denials.
- `test_claude_read_hook_keeps_posix_backslashes_literal` (6 cases): literal backslashes under a POSIX root are never approved, a normal POSIX path still is, and POSIX matching stays case-sensitive.

Against the hook on `main`, the 5 Windows allow cases fail. Against this PR's first revision, the 4 POSIX backslash cases fail. With this revision, all 19 pass.

title: feat(draft): leave architecture choices to the owner
body:
## Contribution Type

  - [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)
  - [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
  - [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

  ## Summary of Key Changes

  Closes #77.

  - **`skills/egm_draft/SKILL.md`: new Execution Constraint 13, "Owner Decides Architecture" (9 lines).** When a design decision has more than one defensible answer, the agent presents up to three options with their mechanism, trade-offs, and failure conditions, and asks the owner to choose through the single-select gate. It does not rank options, mark a default, or pick one. If the owner asks it to choose, it restates the trade-offs and presents the same gate again. Mechanical choices with one defensible answer (file naming, formatting) stay with the agent. Why: when the owner said "pick the best option", `egm_draft` chose the architecture, but the owner has to keep responsibility for decisions that carry their name in review.
  - **`skills/egm_draft/test_scenarios.yaml`: new `owner_delegates_architecture_choice` scenario.** The owner asks the agent to pick twice ("Pick the best option", then "Whatever you think is best, just pick one"). Each reply must ask the owner to choose and must not contain picking phrases. YAML anchors (`&asks_owner`, `&does_not_pick`) keep the two checks written once.

  Differences from the issue's proposal:
  - **Placement:** an Execution Constraint instead of `rules/`, which does not exist, or Step 6, which is the final save step. Execution Constraints apply to every step, including Steps 3–5 where architecture choices come up.
  - **Base:** built on `main`, not stacked on #43, which was closed without merging.

  Live check (manual, not part of CI): the old and new `SKILL.md` were run with `claude -p` (no tools; hooks and CLAUDE.md disabled; a short note told the model it had no tools and should reply in chat), 2 runs per prompt. Sonnet ran every prompt: the issue's wording, "whatever you think is best", "just pick one", no options given, the owner insisting a second time, five candidates, file naming, HTTP 429 vs 500, and owner already chose Redis. Haiku ran a subset.
  - The old skill picked for the owner in 19 of 20 delegation runs. In all 20 runs with the new skill, the agent asked the owner to choose and used no picking phrase. In a separate two-turn check (6 new-skill conversations: 2 Sonnet, 4 Haiku), all 12 turns passed.
  - Exemptions hold. For file naming and for HTTP 429 vs 500, the agent decides itself. When the owner has already chosen Redis, it proceeds without asking again (Sonnet).
  - The first wording, "ask again", let Haiku answer the second "just pick one" with a narrowing question instead of the options in 1 of 2 runs. "Present the same gate again" fixed this (4 of 4 runs).
  - The scenario regexes were built from these outputs. New-skill outputs pass 20 of 20 and old-skill outputs fail 20 of 20.

  Known limits: the regexes match phrases, so a new way of picking could slip through (for example "Decision: Redis" or "I've made the call", which old-skill runs used alongside phrases the regex does catch). The repo has no scenario runner. Testing covered Claude models only, replying in chat without the `ask_question` tool. With more than three candidates, the agent narrows the list; in every run it named the options it cut and why.

  ## Human Accountability Affirmation

  - [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Problem Statement & Motivation

Copilot CLI supports plugins and custom subagents. By default, subagents do not receive repository instructions. Verify this behavior and access to the full EGM package.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### Proposed overview

Add a small host adapter that uses the existing skills, reviewer personas, and document standards. Keep this content shared. Keep this work separate from the release stack.

### Goals

- Install the full package, including agents/ and resources/, through a documented host-specific path.
- Run brainstorm, draft, and review end to end with fixed host and model versions.
- Verify required resource reads, reviewer completion, read-only enforcement, and fresh context with a test marker known only to the parent.
- Keep the human approval steps and output files. Stop clearly when required delegation is unavailable.
- Record the candidate commit, package identity, and host and model versions. Record installation, workflow, and isolation results separately.

### Non-goals

- Copies of skill content, a generic adapter framework, or support claims based only on skill discovery.
- Automatic paid tests, directory publication, or support for other product surfaces.

title: Explain ignored agents folder warning in Claude Code
body:
**Environment:** Claude Code 2.1.310, egm 0.1.0 (commit d651fe8), installed from the `egm` marketplace at user scope.

**What happens:** `/plugin` > Errors lists:

```
egm @ egm (user)
  Default agents/ folder is ignored because the manifest sets "agents"
  Remove "agents" from .claude-plugin/plugin.json (or SKILL.md frontmatter) to auto-load the folder, or add the folder's files
  to the "agents" list if you want both
```

The plugin still works. All nine `.claude-plugin/agents/` adapters load (`egm:egm-style`, `egm:egm-synthesizer`, ...). The persona files in `agents/` are skipped, which is what the design intends (docs/harnesses.md, docs/claude.md).

**Why neither suggested fix works:**

- Removing `"agents"` from `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` would make Claude Code load the `agents/` personas as agents. They use the same names as the adapters (`name: egm-style`) and set no `tools:` restriction, so the read-only Goldfish reviewers would get write tools.
- Listing both folders gives each persona two registrations under the same name.
- Renaming `agents/` would break Antigravity, which loads `agents/` by default (docs/harnesses.md).

**Request:** add a note to docs/claude.md (and the troubleshooting section, if there is one) saying that this error is expected and harmless, so users don't "fix" it by editing the manifest. If you know a supported way to tell Claude Code that `agents/` should be skipped on purpose, using that instead would remove the error entirely.

## Related pull requests

Proposed fix: #127.

title: Add shared workflow tests across supported hosts

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

Host checks use different prompts, scripts, and evidence formats. Claude Code and Codex use `tests/integration/test_claude.py` and `test_codex.py`. Antigravity, Cowork, and ChatGPT used separate scripts in #103.

Each run checks isolation, the line-count fixture, review order, required reads, absence of implementation changes, and equality between draft and final design. Different pass rules prevent direct comparison.

Repeated setup slows revalidation. The round-two changes in #103 did not receive a fresh run on every host.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Define each test case once: prompt, fixture, artifacts, and pass rules. Add a small adapter per host to install the candidate and collect native traces. Use one results schema to generate the `TESTING.md` table and PR reports.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

In scope:

- Eval cases in the repo, with versions. Minimum set: fresh-context isolation (marker probe), full brainstorm, draft, and review on the line-count fixture, review stage order, required reads for each reviewer, no implementation files, final design equal to draft, and the `egm-bootstrap` worker JSON contract.
- One assertion library that reads each native trace format: Claude JSONL, Codex session logs, AGY `stream-json` and child transcripts. It writes the same pass and fail fields for each harness.
- Runner adapters for Antigravity CLI, Claude Code, and Codex CLI. Each runs with an isolated configuration: no user hooks, MCP servers, or other plugins.
- A manual procedure for Cowork and ChatGPT Work. It uses the same cases and a results template.
- A results schema and a generator for the `TESTING.md` harness table.
- Rules for what counts as native evidence and what is only a parent self-report. Take these from the #103 reports.

Out of scope:

- Review quality scores or model output comparisons. This suite checks that the workflow ran correctly. #61 covers quality.
- CI runs against live models.
- New harness support. #60 and `docs/harnesses.md` cover that.

Context: the #103 harness reports, #105, #106, and the AGY live revalidation comment on #103.

## Status review: 2026-10-27

#152 merged and adds stricter Claude persona-read evidence checks plus documentation of evidence limits. Current main still has separate Claude and Codex integration tests; this is partial groundwork, not the shared cases, AGY runner, common results schema/table generator, and manual cloud procedure required here. Keep this issue open. Cloud follow-ups remain #105 and #106; release-level validation remains #60.

title: Store EGM outputs in a dedicated folder

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

EGM writes briefs, drafts, and reports to the working directory or the host's artifact directory. Claude Code has no artifact directory. Review files accumulate at the repository root, where users can commit them by mistake.

@jpettitt raised this in #103: https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/pull/103#discussion_r4352863855. Claude Code deletes its scratchpad with the session. Later stages and `egm-resolve` need earlier reports, so the scratchpad cannot hold persistent artifacts. `docs/claude.md` records the current working-directory behavior.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Add one output folder in the working directory, for example `egm/`. The name is open. All EGM skills write their artifacts there by default. A documented override sets a different folder. Users who do not want the files tracked add one line to `.gitignore`. Files stay readable across sessions and stages.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

In scope:

- One default output location for `egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, `egm-review`, `egm-review-loop`, `egm-resolve`, and `egm-drift-report`.
- A parameter or convention to override the folder.
- Updates to the places where skills look for prior artifacts: `./concepts_brief.md`, `scratch/`, and the conversation artifact directory.
- Matching updates to `docs/claude.md`, `docs/codex.md`, `docs/harnesses.md`, and the `TESTING.md` fixtures.

Out of scope:

- Any temporary directory that belongs to one session.
- Changes to the content or format of the artifacts.
- Harness artifact panes. Antigravity artifacts work as they do today.

## Related pull requests

Partial implementation merged in #118: users can override the artifact directory. The proposed default output location remains unresolved.

title: fix(bootstrap): prevent source-grounding hallucinations
body:
## Contribution Type

Please select the track that matches this pull request:

- [x] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/` or `agents/`; no design doc required)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

## Summary of Key Changes

When `egm-bootstrap` runs on real codebases, it produces README contracts with RPC methods, tables, and invariants inferred from directory or file names. It also cut off large source files at 300 lines, which dropped methods defined further down. This PR tightens grounding and reading in `skills/egm_bootstrap/SKILL.md`:

1. **Scout citation rule (Step 4.1):** `goldfish-explorer` must cite `[file:symbol_or_flag]` for every interface, invariant, and side-effect entry. It may not infer RPC methods, routes, enums, or invariants from file or directory names, and it outputs `["None"]` when the code has no explicit invariants or side effects.
2. **Import and dependency check (Step 4.2):** before attributing an RPC service, schema, or message type to a local file, scouts check build-manifest deps and `import` / `#include` statements.
3. **No read caps; bounded scout chunks instead (Step 4.2):** the 50KB per-directory cap and the 300-line per-file limit are removed. Every non-test file is read in full. To keep any single scout's context bounded, the worker lists top-level definitions with its search tool, cuts the directory's files into chunks of about 1,500 lines at those boundaries (never mid-body; small files share a chunk), spawns one `goldfish-explorer` per chunk in parallel, and merges their JSON. Each chunk receives the file's imports and top-level definition list so it can judge visibility.
4. **Non-test read order (Step 4.2):** contracts, schemas, and build manifests first (extracting exact DDL table names and exported targets); then module entry points and production source/query files; then templates and configs (200 lines each, 800 in config-only directories; stylesheets excluded). Test files (`*_test.*`, `*Test.*`, `test_*.*`, `*.spec.*`) are ignored, including in hybrid directories.
5. **Bazel target syntax:**
   - Step 0 changes `bazel test ...` to `bazel test //...`. A bare `...` is not a valid target pattern.
   - Step 4.2 requires `//pkg/...` or `//pkg:all`, never `//pkg...` or `//pkg:...`.
   - Step 4.2 says to use `bazel run` for interactive runners.
6. **Root diagrams (Step 5.3):** root architecture and sequence diagrams must match the boundaries, operation names, and storage backends in the child `subtree_index` payloads. No unverified nodes.
7. **Final verification (Step 5.4):** checks that contracts cite real symbols, flags, and tables with no speculative claims, and that targets use valid syntax.
8. **Drift review (Step 5.5):** `egm-drift-report` checks for hallucinated content as well as missing coverage, verifying documented methods, routes, enums, tables, and invariants against source and recording discrepancies in the drift report for human triage.
9. **New test scenarios** in `test_scenarios.yaml`:
   - `bootstrap_code_grounding`: requires the `[file:symbol]` citation form and `None` invariants, and forbids invented refund APIs. The prompt does not contain the expected symbol, so the model can't pass by repeating the prompt.
   - `bootstrap_bazel_target_syntax`: requires `//pkg/a/...` or `//pkg/a:all` and forbids bare `...`, `//pkg...`, and `//pkg:...`.
10. **Templates moved to `references/templates.md`:** the three README templates are unchanged but now live beside `references/worker-return.schema.json`, and `SKILL.md` tells the agent to read them before writing any contract. This keeps the loaded skill body at 23,609 bytes, under the 24,000-byte limit that `tests/unit/test_skill_load_limits.py` (from #114) enforces; `main` is already at 23,504, so any addition to this skill needed this. Per reviewer guidance, detail moved into an explicitly read reference file rather than raising the limit.

**Review follow-up (@briansuchy, @n3wth):** the 250KB directory cap and the 1,500-line entry-point limit from the earlier revision are gone. Nothing is skipped or truncated; 1,500 lines is now the size of a scout chunk, not a limit on what is read. Entry points and production files follow the same rule. The scope advisory will count `references/templates.md` as a second core file; it is the relocated template block, not new instructions.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

- [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Verification

- [ ] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Executed `/egm-review docs/designs/<name>.md`, resolved findings via `/egm-resolve`, and verified relative links (`pytest tests/unit/test_link_integrity.py`).
- [x] **For Bug Fix / Implementation PRs (Stage 2)**: Unit tests or `test_scenarios.yaml` added/updated and `pytest tests/unit` executed.
- [ ] **For Harness Support PRs**: Verified plugin installation and end-to-end execution of `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` on the target harness; attached execution summary or transcript.

**What was and wasn't verified:**

- `pytest tests/unit` on this revision: 50 pass, 0 fail (includes `test_skill_load_limits.py`; see item 10).
- The repo has no eval runner, so the new scenarios are structurally valid but have not been run against a model.
- **Manual before/after run (this revision).** I ran `egm-bootstrap` once with the `main` skill and once with this branch's skill, each by a fresh agent that did not know which version it had, on identical copies of a small Bazel/Python fixture: 4 packages, direct-execution mode (≤5 dirs), scouts spawned as real read-only subagents. The fixture includes `ledger/ledger.py` (408 lines; public API at lines 392–399), `ingest/pipeline.py` (1,965 lines; `parse_batch` at 336, `BatchWriter` at 986, `MAX_RETRIES_FLAG` at 1,736, `RetryExhausted` at 1,940, `flush_all` at 1,944, checkpoint write at 1,963), a test file with a decoy `FakeSink` class in the same directory, a `refund_service/` holding only `format_currency`, and a `billing/` client importing the external `ChargeServiceStub`. Results:

| Check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `ingest/pipeline.py` symbols past line 300 (`parse_batch`, `BatchWriter`) | Missed; scout read lines 1–300, README says "not yet documented" | Documented |
| `ingest/pipeline.py` symbols past line 1,500 (`MAX_RETRIES_FLAG`, `RetryExhausted`, `flush_all`, checkpoint write) | Missed; side effect listed as "Unverified" | Documented, incl. retry bound, checkpoint-after-success ordering, and that nothing parses `MAX_RETRIES_FLAG` |
| Scout calls for `ingest/` | 1 (lines 1–300) | 2 parallel chunks (1–1,006 and 1,007–1,965), cut at the top-level boundary before `_write_sink`, merged |
| `ledger/ledger.py` public API below line 390 | Documented, but only because that scout ignored the 300-line cap (read 409 lines) | Documented |
| `[file:symbol]` citations across 5 READMEs | 0 | 52 |
| Invariants for a pure helper with none in code | 4 inferred properties | `None explicit in code` |
| `refund_service/` holding only a currency formatter | No invented refund API | No invented refund API; README states none exists |
| External `ChargeServiceStub` | External | External, with the `@payments_api//v1` build dep cited |
| Test-only `FakeSink` leaked into a contract | No | No |
| Valid Bazel target patterns | Yes | Yes |
| READMEs admitting unread or unverified code | 2 | 0 |

- **How to read this:** the chunking rule is what changed `ingest/`; everything past line 300 was invisible to `main`'s scout and everything past line 1,500 would have been invisible to this PR's previous revision. The `ledger` row shows `main`'s cap being violated by the scout rather than honored, so `main` reading that file fully is not a point in its favor. Name-inference, external-attribution, test-filtering, and Bazel checks already passed on `main` with this model, so for those the PR tightens instructions without a measured improvement. One run per version; evidence, not a benchmark.
- **Not covered by any run:** a directory whose total source exceeds one chunk across many small files (batching several files into one scout), the parallel worker swarm (>5 directories), pre-existing README correction, root diagram matching (Step 5.3), the drift-report audit (Step 5.5), and tier-3 configs.

body:
## Contribution Type

- [ ] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch**
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR**
- [x] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #8`)

## Summary of Key Changes

This PR adds plugin packaging and guides for Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Codex CLI, and ChatGPT Work. It removes the old Gemini CLI packaging. Antigravity CLI (`agy`) replaces it.

- Adds Claude and Codex manifests and marketplace entries. The shared personas stay host-neutral. Thin Claude adapters restrict reviewer tools and exclude the project CLAUDE.md context. The synthesizer also has a Claude adapter with `tools: [Agent, Read, Grep, Glob, Write]`. It can start reviewers and write reports. It does not get Bash, Edit, or MCP connectors.
- All seven skill entry points point to the correct harness guide. Each guide covers four topics: how to find installed resources, which native tools exist, direct dispatch when nesting is not available, and the required persona, target, and standard reads.
- A live run showed that Claude started review stages in parallel. The Claude guide now requires stages 5 to 9 in sequence. A new native run confirmed the fix.
- Commit f4d342c applies the review notes from @jpettitt (Claude Code 2.1.306). The no-nesting rule now applies to Claude Cowork only. Claude Code nests up to 3 levels, so the synthesizer can dispatch there. The guide tells the model to read `SKILL.md` for chained EGM skills, because the `Skill` tool refuses `disable-model-invocation` skills. The guide also says that persona and standard reads from the plugin cache prompt the user in interactive sessions. In headless sessions these reads fail without `--allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob` or `permissions.allow` rules. A `PreToolUse` hook for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` will come in a follow-up PR. Commit d0d0125 adds a Claude adapter for the bootstrap orchestrator. The adapter sends workers to the bootstrap `SKILL.md`. A probe showed that the bare persona skipped the skill and returned prose, not the JSON `subtree_index`. The guide now also says: Claude Code has no artifact comments, reviewers cannot open URLs, and deliverables go to the working directory, not the session scratchpad.
- Both native trace readers split JSONL on a literal LF. Regression tests cover valid Unicode separators inside JSON strings. The earlier report of malformed exports was wrong. The correction is below.
- Documentation navigation is in one place. Repeated rubric descriptions are removed. `resources/` stays the single source for standards. The full verification reports are in this PR. `TESTING.md` has a short run table. The removed verification and design documents are not restored.
- Updates the `README.md` installation steps and the philosophy text. Landing site (`site/`) changes: the hero has one subtitle and a `Copy install prompt` button. The essay credit is now in the Model section. The agent prompt is separate from the CLI copy boxes for Antigravity, Claude Code with Claude Cowork, and Codex. The separate Essay section is removed. The earlier copy and screenshot pass is in [#107](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/pull/107). The screenshots here were made again after the merge of main, so they show the #108 logo. Before and after captures are collapsed below.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

- [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Verification

- [ ] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Not applicable to this implementation track. The earlier review targeted a design document that the author removed during consolidation. It does not verify the current files.
- [x] **For Bug Fix / Implementation PRs (Stage 2)**: `pytest tests`: 22 passed, 3 opt-in live tests skipped. The synthesizer and bootstrap adapter tests are new. The live commands ran separately, as reported below. Astro check: 15 files, zero errors, warnings, or hints. The static build and the screenshot capture passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- [ ] **For Harness Support PRs**: Full support verification is still partial. Codex passed both native tests. The Claude full fixture completed. Its stage-order fix passed a focused rerun. ChatGPT completed all native reviewers. Its final artifact audit is still open. The Cowork fresh run reached the usage limit after stage 7. The AGY isolation probe and the full fixture passed in a temporary HOME. See the report in the comments. Packaging and reviewer completion are not proof of full isolation or end-to-end verification.

## Current result by harness

| Harness | Result | Remaining boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code 2.1.308 | Isolation passed. The full fixture completed. Nine native reviewers verified the stage-order fix. | Approvals were simulated. The parent broke the no-shell fixture rule. The extra consolidated report was not written. The process needed cleanup after the final result. Not run live again: synthesizer-nested dispatch, the bootstrap adapter, and the guide changes made after review. |
| Codex CLI 0.163.0 | Two live tests passed. 15 native reviewers ran in ordered stages. Required reads and matching artifacts are verified. | Interactive approvals and nesting were not tested. |
| Claude Cowork / Opus 5.5 Medium | Installed. Brainstorm, draft, and review stages 5 to 7 completed. | The usage limit stopped stage 8. Stage 9, the exports, and the canary child output are not verified. See #105. |
| ChatGPT Work / GPT-6.1 Sol Light | The installed candidate hashes matched. The native UI shows the probe answer UNKNOWN and 15 completed workflow reviewers. | The final artifact audit, the state after resolution, and the full child tool traces are not verified. See #106. |
| Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 | The isolation probe passed on the native child transcript. The full fixture ran with 16 native reviewers. Stages 5 to 9 ran in sequence by timestamp. All required reads occurred. Five stage reports exist. No code was written. Report in comments, candidate d0d0125. | The final design differs from the draft in one `Status` line. Not tested: interactive approvals, `egm-bootstrap`, and synthesizer nesting. The bootstrap skill is larger than the load limit. |

The temporary CLI installations are removed. A browser takeover stopped the cloud artifact export and cleanup. The two task-only cloud plugins are still installed and enabled until browser access resumes. No usage reset or credit purchase was made.

Known gaps stay open in [#105](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/105) and [#106](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/106). The site audit reports two high dependency findings that existed before this PR. The package file and the lockfile are the same as the PR base. The full evidence and the exact candidate limits follow. Later site-only commits do not mean that the native tests ran again on those commits.

title: feat: install EGM on Claude Code (draft for #8)
body:
## Contribution Type

- [ ] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch**
- [ ] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR**
- [x] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Refs #8`)

No track fits cleanly yet: #8 hasn't been triaged. The change touches no files in `skills/` or `agents/`, but it is over 100 non-test lines, so it falls on the feature track. I ticked Stage 2 so the template check can run. If you'd rather start with a design doc, I'll turn this into a Stage 1 PR.

## Summary of Key Changes

This adds Claude Code as a harness without changing any shared skill or persona file:

```text
/plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
/plugin install egm@elephant-goldfish-model
```

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `marketplace.json`: the manifests. Claude Code loads `skills/` as usual.
- `.claude-plugin/agents/*.md`: one short wrapper per persona, with the same `name` and `description`. Each wrapper tells the agent to read its persona from `agents/`, so the persona text isn't duplicated. The reviewer wrappers allow only `Read, Grep, Glob` and set `omitClaudeMd: true`. That enforces the "Strict Read-Only Protocol" the personas already describe, and keeps the user's `CLAUDE.md` out of a Goldfish review. These keys can't go in `agents/` itself: Antigravity rejects `tools: Read, Grep, Glob` and skips the agent. I checked this with `agy plugin validate`, and with a live run that failed with `tool "Read" not found in registry`.
- A `UserPromptSubmit` hook in `plugin.json`: when a prompt starts with `/egm:`, it tells the agent the plugin root. Claude Code installs plugins outside the project, so without this the skills' relative `agents/` and `resources/` paths resolve against the user's repo. It also points the agent to the new section in `docs/harnesses.md`. Other prompts get nothing.
- `docs/harnesses.md`: Claude Code rows in the three tables, and a "Claude Code" section that maps the skills onto Claude Code tools (Agent, AskUserQuestion, chained skills, the bootstrap scout).
- `README.md` and `docs/getting_started.md`: list Claude Code among the harnesses.
- `tests/unit/test_claude_code.py`: checks that every persona has a matching wrapper and that reviewers stay read-only. It also checks that no Claude-only key leaks into `agents/`, that every `egm-*` name the skills dispatch to exists, and that the manifests agree.

Questions for you:

1. `egm-review` tells the agent to invoke `egm-review-loop` and `egm-resolve`. All skills set `disable-model-invocation: true`, so Claude Code's Skill tool refuses those calls. The guide tells the agent to read the other skill's `SKILL.md` and follow it in the same thread. The alternative is to drop the flag from those two skills, which would affect every harness. Which do you prefer?
2. Claude Code names commands after the skill folder, so users type `/egm:egm_review`. Antigravity also warns that the folder names don't match the `name` fields. Renaming the folders to `egm-review` and so on would fix both, but it touches links on egm.dev, so I left it out.

Two things I found on `main` while testing, unrelated to this change:

- Gemini CLI 0.65.0's agent loader rejects every persona in `agents/`. It validates frontmatter strictly, and `license` isn't an allowed key: `Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'license'`.
- `skills/egm_bootstrap/SKILL.md` is 24,489 bytes, and Antigravity loads only the first 24,000.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

- [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Verification

- [ ] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Executed `/egm-review docs/designs/<name>.md`, resolved findings via `/egm-resolve`, and verified relative links (`pytest tests/unit/test_link_integrity.py`).
- [x] **For Bug Fix / Implementation PRs (Stage 2)**: Unit tests or `test_scenarios.yaml` added/updated and `pytest tests/unit` executed.
- [ ] **For Harness Support PRs**: Verified plugin installation and end-to-end execution of `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` on the target harness; attached execution summary or transcript.

I left the harness box unticked because the runs below were headless. An interactive run is still to do.

- `pytest tests/unit` passes. Mutation checks: renaming, duplicating, or deleting a wrapper, or adding `Bash` to a reviewer, each fails a test.
- `claude plugin validate .` passes. `agy plugin validate --strict` reports exactly the same warnings as on `main`. Antigravity 1.4.4 with this branch installed spawned `egm-zoom-out`, and it read a file as before.
- Isolation probe, on Claude Code 2.1.306 loading this branch with `--plugin-dir` ([script](https://github.com/kurcontko/egm-claude-code/blob/main/tests/live_probe.py)):
  - The workspace `CLAUDE.md` and the parent prompt each held a random marker.
  - `/egm:egm_review` read `docs/harnesses.md` from the plugin root and spawned one new `egm:egm-zoom-out`, not a fork.
  - The reviewer saw neither marker, and its tools were `Read, Grep, Glob`.
- End to end on this branch, on a small sample repo, headless, taking the first option at each question:
  - The hook fired on each `/egm:` prompt.
  - Brainstorm: `egm:egm-synthesizer` spawned six `egm:egm-*` reviewers one level down, and the brief was written.
  - Draft: wrote `docs/designs/due-dates.md` in the workspace. The plugin's own `docs/designs/` was untouched.
  - Review (fresh session): wrote all five stage reports from 17 subagent runs, all `egm:` agents, none forked. Reviewers only read. Only the synthesizer wrote files.
  - A stage 7 run on its own read `skills/egm_review_loop/SKILL.md` from the plugin root and followed it, so the chained-skill rule works.

Written with Claude Code.

title: Present design trade-offs without choosing for the owner

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation
`egm_draft` does not prevent the agent from choosing an architecture when the owner says "pick the best option". The owner must retain responsibility for architectural decisions.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview
Add a short rule in `rules/` or `egm_draft` Step 6. Present up to three options with their mechanisms, trade-offs, and failure conditions. Use the existing single-select gate. Do not rank options or select a default. If the owner asks the agent to choose, restate the trade-offs and request a decision.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals
In scope:

- Rule text, under 10 lines, plus one `test_scenarios.yaml` case where the owner says "just pick one".
- Stacks on PR #43.

Out of scope:

- Mechanical choices with one defensible answer (file naming, formatting). The rule applies to decisions that will carry the owner's name in review.
- Changing `egm_brainstorm`, which already produces divergent options by design.

title: Add an optional whiteboard check before spec verification

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation
EGM reviews the design but does not check the owner's understanding. Owners need to explain the mechanism, trade-offs, and failure modes before they approve a design.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview
Add an optional whiteboard gate after findings are resolved and before verification, in `egm_review_loop` or `egm_resolve` Step 6. A fresh Goldfish reads only the design and asks three questions, one at a time:

- How does the core mechanism work, and how can it fail?
- Where is the performance or cost bottleneck?
- Why was the simplest alternative rejected?

The owner answers in chat. The Goldfish reports answers that conflict with the design. The result prompts a review; it does not block approval.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals
In scope:

- One new optional step, off by default, enabled by a parameter or a one-line rule.
- Reuses the existing `comprehension` Goldfish persona with a `Mode: WHITEBOARD` branch.
- Stacks on PR #43 (sign-off focus prompts in `egm_draft` Step 6), which already surfaces the hardest trade-off and lowest-confidence area.

Out of scope:

- Any scoring, pass/fail threshold, or record of the owner's answers.
- Making the gate mandatory. The FAQ already defends against turning design review into a bottleneck.
- Course or training content. This is a tooling step, not a lesson.

title: Resume interrupted reviews safely

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

Interrupted reviews can repeat work and model calls. Reused results can become stale when inputs or reviewer definitions change.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

First document representative interruptions, then design minimal persisted stage state keyed to relevant inputs and reviewer configuration. Resume only compatible completed work.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

**Acceptance criteria:** Resume skips valid completed stages; changed inputs or configuration invalidate affected results; partial writes and concurrent runs are handled; users can force a clean run; fresh reviewer context is preserved.

**Non-goals:** No workflow engine, cross-machine sync, or reuse of stale findings merely because filenames match.

## Related work

Coordinate with runtime limits. Defer implementation unless interruption evidence justifies the added state complexity.

Maintainer scope approval is required before a design or implementation PR.

title: Add explicit review runtime limits

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

Long reviews need predictable stopping behavior and useful partial output when a run reaches its limits.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Define reviewer-call and elapsed-time limits, preserve completed findings, and report the reason for stopping. Distinguish host-enforced limits from prompt-only requests.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

**Goals / acceptance criteria:** Define limit accounting including retries; verify stop behavior at boundaries; preserve completed outputs; report unsupported enforcement honestly; show cost only when reliable usage and pricing are available.

**Non-goals:** No claim of a hard spending cap from prompt instructions and no billing integration.

## Related work

Coordinate with interrupted-run recovery, while keeping limit behavior independently specified.

## Next step

Proposal for maintainer triage. Align on scope before a design or implementation PR; this issue does not claim design approval.

title: Benchmark EGM review quality against a baseline

## Problem Statement & Motivation

A complete workflow does not prove review quality. Compare EGM with a baseline for useful findings, time, and token use.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Create a small set of seeded design defects and compare a normal review with EGM under documented, comparable conditions and repeated runs.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

**Acceptance criteria:** Report defects caught, false positives, elapsed time, and available token usage; use a documented human scoring rubric; record model and prompt versions; report variability and limitations.

**Non-goals:** No leaderboard, broad model ranking, or LLM judge as the sole source of truth.

## Related work

Complements existing evaluation work in #47, #48, and #50. Start after the integrated host workflows stabilize.

title: Verify exact release bundles across supported hosts
body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

Finish validation of the exact tagged release artifacts users receive. Build on the completed candidate testing; do not repeat historical tests merely to recreate evidence.

## Completed groundwork

Merged PR #103 records installation, workflow, and reviewer-isolation testing for pinned candidates, including host/model versions and bundle identity evidence where available. Its reports distinguish passes, failures, and unverified behavior.

- Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Antigravity have candidate-level test evidence in #103.
- Cowork and ChatGPT Work have partial candidate evidence. Remaining cloud workflow, artifact-audit, and isolation gaps stay tracked in #105 and #106.
- Merged #136 supplies runtime packaging and targeted permission/isolation checks (replacing #120).
- Merged #137 supplies versioned archives, checksums, and draft-release preparation for completed #124 (replacing #128 and the earlier #125 work).

These records count as groundwork. They do not establish that a later tagged artifact is identical to the tested candidate or passes on every host.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Define and execute the remaining release-candidate procedure against the exact tagged bundle. Record source SHA, tag, archive checksum, installed artifact identity, host/model versions, date, and separate installation, workflow, and isolation outcomes.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

Remaining acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Document reproducible clean-install and validation commands for the release artifacts.
- [x] Identify the exact tag, source commit, and archive checksums produced by the release process (v0.1.0 release notes).
- [ ] Verify that installed files on each tested host match the intended release artifact.
- [ ] Run the release-level checks needed for the hosts claimed as supported by that release. Reuse #103's fixtures and reports; explain any carried-forward evidence and its applicability instead of treating old candidate results as new release passes.
- [ ] Record installation, workflow, and isolation outcomes separately, with failures, limitations, and untested hosts explicit.
- [ ] Require explicit invocation for paid live tests; do not add automatic paid runs to every PR.
- [x] Attach artifact identities and offline/provenance validation evidence to the corresponding release notes.
- [ ] Attach the exact installed-artifact host validation report to the corresponding release notes.

Non-goals: repeating the entire historical test campaign, promising universal model support, implementing release packaging again, or duplicating the cloud follow-ups in #105 and #106. Unresolved cloud gaps must remain visible and constrain release support claims.

## Dependencies and Related Work

Completed release packaging/preparation: #135, #136, #137, and #124. Candidate verification evidence: #103. Cloud follow-ups: #105 and #106.

Earlier groundwork: #46, #49, #51, #55, and #56. GitHub release guidance: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases

Keep this issue open until the release-level criteria above are met. Maintainer scope approval is required before a design or implementation PR.

## Related pull requests

Current release prerequisites: #135 (design), #136 (packaging, replacing #120), and #137 (release automation, replacing #128). These do not complete this issue's exact-artifact host verification.


## Status review: 2026-10-27

Release preparation is complete: #135, #136, and #137 merged, #124 is closed, and [v0.1.0](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/releases/tag/v0.1.0) contains both runtime ZIPs and checksums. Exact installed-artifact host verification remains open in #60.

v0.1.0 source: `b3a35956759bf7f024af2ff061b2e0b44b438e4c`. Release workflow [40468086866](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/actions/runs/40468086866) succeeded for build, attestation, artifact transfer, and draft creation. Published notes record both archive checksums and successful source/provenance checks, while explicitly stating no live host tests ran against these exact ZIPs. The first release is therefore available for this issue to validate; preparation is no longer a blocker. Historical candidate passes remain separate.

title: Add a TRIZ design-review persona

labels.name: design-ready
labels.description: Maintainer-approved inquiry unlocked for an EGM Design Document PR

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation
Software system design is routinely constrained by perceived trade-offs—such as throughput versus durability, flexibility versus simplicity, or speed versus correctness. Engineers and AI drafting agents frequently accept these compromises as inevitable laws of architecture. Within the Elephant & Goldfish Model (EGM), existing Goldfish personas are predominantly evaluative: they effectively audit designs for bottlenecks, unstated assumptions, YAGNI violations, and structural consistency, but none actively challenge the *premise* of an architectural compromise or offer structural patterns to resolve it.

Integrating the TRIZ method (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) introduces an inventive, transformative dimension to EGM. By systematically identifying underlying technical contradictions and applying recognized software architecture patterns (such as Inversion of Control, Segmentation, Intermediaries, and Preliminary Actions), EGM can challenge false compromises and propose concrete structural transforms to achieve the Ideal Final Result without ungrounded over-engineering.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)
### 1. Proposed Overview

Introduce a new dedicated Goldfish persona, **"The Inventive Catalyst"** (`agents/inventive_catalyst.md`), to the open-source EGM framework. The persona operates with an inlined reference catalog of 10 curated software engineering TRIZ principles (with mandatory secondary operational trade-offs) for self-contained, zero-I/O execution across all supported agent harnesses. It integrates upstream into `/egm-brainstorm`'s shootdown swarm (expanding from 6 to 7 specialized lenses) and into the review workflow to unearth false compromises in proposed architectures.

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals
**In-Scope Goals:**
* **Dedicated Persona Definition**: Create `agents/inventive_catalyst.md` with read-only mandates, stateless isolation, inlined software patterns, and structured output schemas for ideation and review.
* **Brainstorm Swarm Integration**: Add `egm-inventive-catalyst` to the parallel shootdown swarm in `skills/egm_brainstorm/SKILL.md` (updating the lens table and `concepts_brief.md` template to 7 lenses) and update `agents/synthesizer.md` to dispatch and compile contradiction analysis.
* **Review-Time Contradiction Auditing**: Integrate contradiction analysis into the design review workflow without creating blocking repair loops or cyclic whiplash with simplicity checks (`egm-zoom-out`).

**Out-of-Scope Non-Goals:**
* **Modifying Existing Personas**: Modifying or diluting existing single-responsibility personas (`design_critic`, `zoom_out`, etc.) with TRIZ logic.
* **External Redundant Catalogs**: Creating external reference encyclopedias (`resources/triz_patterns.md`) that are not read at runtime, avoiding dual-maintenance drift debt.
* **Pipeline Renumbering**: Altering the canonical 5-phase review sequence numbering (Steps 5–9).
