title: feat(site): integrate editorial illustrations from foundational essay
body:
## Summary
This draft PR audits the `egm.dev` landing site (`site/`) and introduces editorial illustrations directly derived from Dave Rensin's foundational essay, ["Elephants, Goldfish, and the New Golden Age of Software Engineering"](https://drensin.medium.com/elephants-goldfish-and-the-new-golden-age-of-software-engineering-c33641a48874).

## Identified Opportunities & Changes

### 1. `site/src/components/Essay.astro` (Primary Editorial Feature)
- **Previous state**: A bare text-only callout with a headline and link to Medium.
- **Opportunity**: The essay is the intellectual origin of the model. Featuring the original editorial illustration here visually demonstrates the core thesis ("Design is the New Code", the Elephant holding the "Source of Truth" scroll, and the Goldfish review swarm).
- **Change**: Embedded the full 16:9 illustration inside an adaptive, rounded container (`--md-sys-shape-corner-lg`), subtle border, responsive 2-column layout on desktop, and a caption attributing the artwork.

### 2. `site/src/components/Model.astro` (Role Avatars / Spot Badges)
- **Previous state**: Generic geometric SVG circle glyphs (a solid circle for Elephant, an outline ring for Goldfish).
- **Opportunity**: Replace the abstract circles with character spot illustrations from the editorial artwork.
- **Change**: Replaced the geometric circle glyphs with rounded badge containers displaying:
  - **The Elephant**: Deep-context agent wearing utility vest, holding blueprints ("Design Intent", "The Why") and the "Source of Truth" scroll.
  - **The Goldfish**: The Goldfish swarm in action reviewing technical plans and checklists.

### 3. Static Assets (`site/public/images/`)
- Added `drensin-elephant-goldfish.webp` (full editorial illustration, 960x540).
- Added `spot-elephant.webp` (400x400 spot illustration).
- Added `spot-goldfish.webp` (400x400 spot illustration).

## Tradeoffs & Discussion Points for Reviewers
1. **Model section aesthetic**: Do we want the spot character badges in `Model.astro`, or do maintainers prefer the minimalist geometric SVG circles with the illustration reserved exclusively for the `Essay.astro` section?
2. **Open Graph / Social preview**: `site/public/og.png` is currently a plain text card. We can also compose an updated social card featuring the Elephant and Goldfish characters if desired.

title: test: resolve the link-integrity ignore filter against the repo root
body:
## Summary

title: fix(site): uniform state-layer corners on skills rows
body:
## Summary

On hover, the first and last rows of the skills index drew their state layer with square outer corners and rounded inner corners.

Cause: the gBreeze list stylesheet makes a list's first and last rows inherit the list's own corner radii. The index sets the list radius to 0 so the hairline above it runs straight, which the end rows then inherited. Pinning each row's `border-radius` to its own `--container-shape` token makes all four corners equal in every state.

One declaration plus a comment in `site/src/components/Skills.astro`.

title: feat(site): index layout for skills, continuous step rule, section rhythm
body:
## Summary

Layout pass on the landing site after review of the full-page screenshots. No copy changes except one restructured sentence (see below) and one whitespace bug fix.

### Skills: index, not cards

- Hairline rows instead of a stack of filled cards.
- The command moves from an overline above the name into its own 15rem column, so the seven commands read as one aligned list. Its baseline sits on the title's first line (`align-items: baseline`).
- Wraps to command / name / description on narrow screens.
- Fixes a dropped space in the lead: Astro trims the line break before an inline element, which rendered "nolock-in".

### Loop: one continuous rule

- The four steps share a single hairline; each number sits on the rule behind a surface-colored ring (badge `outline`), so the line reads as one sequence.
- The weekly drift check becomes a fifth entry on the same rule with an outlined marker, replacing the trailing paragraph with an inline chip.
- **Copy flag:** that paragraph is restructured as a title plus body: "Then weekly" / `/egm-drift-report` / "Flags where the code and the spec have drifted apart. You pick which one moves." The README sentence it mirrors is unchanged in meaning; say if you want the original wording back.

### Essay: aside register

Two columns at wide widths: headline left, argument and button right, first baselines aligned. Collapses to one column below 820px. Uses the tight step of the section scale.

### Section rhythm

One three-step scale in `global.css` (`--section-y-tight`, `--section-y`, `--section-y-loose`) replaces per-section padding values. The install section enters loose (change of register from light to dark) and exits standard.

## Verification

- `npm run check` (0 errors, 0 warnings) and `npm run build` clean.
- Screenshots at 1440 and 375, light and dark. `site/screenshots/full-light.png` updated.
- DOM checks: skills rows 7; command/title baseline delta 0.45px; essay headline/lead baseline delta 1px; step rule continuous with badges centered on it; no horizontal overflow at 375 (`scrollWidth === innerWidth`); zero console errors.

No new dependencies. Theme values stay on gBreeze tokens; layout overrides on list internals are scoped to the skills section.

title: [Feature]: Install EGM on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

EGM installs cleanly only where someone copies the repository by hand. Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity all read Agent Skills (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`). But each one finds skills, subagents, and plugins through its own paths and manifests.

Two things block this today:

1. No manifests. None of the per-harness plugin or marketplace files exist.
2. The skills name one harness's tools: `invoke_subagent`, `define_subagent`, `write_to_file`, `view_file`, `ask_question`, `list_dir`, artifact metadata, and a "side panel". Seven of the eight skills do this. On other harnesses the model has to guess what was meant. Also, the skills ask for subagents named `egm-design` and `egm-zoom-out`, but the persona frontmatter names are `design-critic` and `zoom-out`.

## Proposed Scope

In scope:

- Make the repository the marketplace for every harness. Manifests point at the repository root (`"source": "./"`).
- Make `agents` a symlink to `personas/`. Rename the persona `name` values to the `egm-*` names the skills already use.
- Add a Delegation section to the four orchestrating skills, and rewrite tool names in harness-neutral words. Behaviour does not change.
- Add `docs/harnesses.md` (install, manifests, subagent mapping, nesting caveats), a README install table, and a per-harness test record in `TESTING.md`.

Out of scope:

- Directory and store listings (Claude directory, OpenAI plugin directory, Cursor Marketplace). These need publisher accounts and reviews.
- ChatGPT web. It has Skills but no subagents, so a Goldfish review cannot run in a fresh context.
- Skill-only installers such as `npx skills add`. They copy `skills/` without `personas/`, `rules/`, and `resources/`, which breaks EGM.

## Validation

Run `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` end to end through each harness's plugin install, and record each run in `TESTING.md`. Claude Code is the priority.

body:
## Problem Statement & Motivation

egm.dev introduces EGM but lacks a complete guide. Existing material lives in `docs/getting_started.md`, `docs/faq.md`, and skill design documents. Turn it into a guide with installation, a worked example, explicit limits, and an author. Reference: https://every.to/guides/ai-product-management-guide.

Add a separate page that renders the existing documents. Avoid duplicate content.

## Proposed Scope (Goals vs. Non-Goals)

### 1. Proposed Overview

Build `egm.dev/guide` in `site/` with an Astro content collection that reads `../docs`. Put installation first. Add a sticky contents list and author byline. Reuse the landing page's gBreeze components and zero-telemetry rules. Link the guide from its navigation and footer.

Content, in order:

1. Install and first run (from the README quickstart and `docs/getting_started.md`).
2. The core loop, brainstorm → draft → review → resolve → build, as a worked example on one real feature with the agent's actual output, trimmed. This is the main deliverable and needs a sanitized transcript and an author who uses EGM daily.
3. Drift detection and bootstrapping an existing codebase (already in `docs/getting_started.md`).
4. FAQ (`docs/faq.md`).
5. Not included: what EGM deliberately does not do, and where it is used today (wording to be settled before publishing).

### 2. Goals vs. Non-Goals

In scope:

- One new Astro page plus a content-collection loader for `docs/`; no copy duplicated into `site/src`.
- A worked example with real, trimmed agent output.
- Byline, sticky table of contents, install block first.

Out of scope:

- Changing the landing page beyond adding a nav and footer link.
- Analytics, newsletter capture, cookie banners, accounts, or any third-party scripts.
- Multi-page docs sites or search; one page is the point.
- Rewriting `docs/getting_started.md` for the web beyond what renders cleanly.

Defer the transcript and final text until after launch. The page template estimate is one day.

title: feat(site): egm.dev landing page and GitHub Pages deploy
body:
## What

Adds the public landing site for https://egm.dev under `site/`, plus the GitHub Pages deploy workflow and a Website badge in the README.

- One static page built with Astro. No client framework, one short clipboard script.
- gBreeze (`@material/web@2.5.0`, `labs/gb`) in its native-element form: the page emits the package class names (`btn`, `icon-btn`, `list-item`, `badge`, `divider`) and imports the package stylesheets. No custom elements, no Lit runtime. Theme comes only from gBreeze tokens (`site/src/styles/tokens.css`) and the components' documented custom properties.
- Google Sans Flex and Google Sans Code self-hosted (OFL). Light by default, follows the system dark scheme, with a forced dark install band and footer.
- Sections: hero, the model (Elephant, Goldfish, Human), the loop, the seven-skill catalog (names and commands identical to the README table, each row deep-links to its `skills/` folder), essay link, install, and a footer with the Apache 2.0 notice, the "not an officially supported Google product" disclaimer, and Google privacy and terms links.

## Why

Launch surface for the open-source release. DNS for `egm.dev` is being pointed at GitHub Pages separately; domain verification on the GitHub org is in progress.

## Zero telemetry

The site makes no requests to Google hosts and loads no third-party resources. Verified on the built output: every absolute URL points at github.com, medium.com, policies.google.com, antigravity.google, geminicli.com, adk.dev, a2a-protocol.org, or egm.dev; zero external resource loads at runtime; one inline script; no cookies. Please keep it that way. It is a condition of the release.

## Deploy and launch-day steps

`.github/workflows/deploy-site.yml` builds `site/` and publishes to GitHub Pages on pushes to `main` that touch `site/`, and on manual dispatch. All actions are SHA-pinned. On launch day, once the repository is public: Settings > Pages > Source = GitHub Actions, custom domain `egm.dev`, Enforce HTTPS, then run the workflow once by hand.

## Verification

- `npm run check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings. `npm run build`: 1 page.
- Output: `index.html` about 25 KB (5.6 KB gzip), one CSS file 48 KB (7.8 KB gzip), two woff2 fonts, `og.png`, `CNAME`, `robots.txt`, `favicon.svg`.
- Computed styles confirm the package styles apply unmodified (filled pill 56 px, radius 28 px, primary background; seven list rows on surface-container-low; forced dark band resolves through `light-dark()`).

title: feat(governance): add OSS PR triage, AI policy, and two-stage EGM design workflow
body:
## Contribution Type

Please select the track that matches this pull request:

- [ ] **Bug Fix / Minor Patch** (Targeted fix, non-test diff <= 100 lines and < 3 core files in `skills/`, `personas/`, `rules/`; no design doc required)
- [x] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 1: Design Doc PR** (`Refs #___` with `status: approved-for-design` | Adds `docs/designs/<name>.md` and updates `docs/designs/README.md`; use `Refs` instead of `Closes` so the issue stays open for Stage 2)
- [x] **Feature / Architectural Change -- Stage 2: Implementation PR** (`Closes #___` with `status: approved-for-pr` | Implements merged `docs/designs/<name>.md`)

## Summary of Key Changes

List all key changes made in this pull request and why:

1. **`AI_POLICY.md` (New)**: Establishes human-in-the-loop accountability rules for AI-assisted contributions, prohibition of autonomous PR creation, two-stage EGM alignment (`status: approved-for-design` -> Stage-1 Design Doc PR -> `status: approved-for-pr` -> Stage-2 Implementation PR), and anti-bloat scope hygiene.
2. **`AGENTS.md` (New)**: Defines hard operational constraints for coding agents acting in the repository (no autonomous `git push` / `gh pr create`, strict adherence to the two-stage EGM design workflow for features, and surgical scope discipline).
3. **`CONTRIBUTING.md` (Updated)**: Documents the dual-track contribution workflow (Track 1: Bug Fix / Minor Patch vs. Track 2: Feature / Architectural Change with two-stage alignment) and links to `AI_POLICY.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
4. **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (New)**: Adds contribution track selection checkboxes (Bug Fix, Stage-1 Design Doc PR, Stage-2 Implementation PR), key change summary, human accountability affirmation, and verification checklist.
5. **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_proposal.md` (New)**: Adds the Feature Inquiry Issue template (`feature-inquiry`, `needs-triage`) for contributors to reach out to maintainers before drafting an EGM design document.
6. **`.github/workflows/pr-scope-advisory.yml` (New)**: Adds a non-blocking GitHub Actions workflow (`pull_request_target`) that evaluates PRs on the Bug Fix / Minor Patch track (>100 non-test/non-doc lines, >=3 core files in `skills/`, `personas/`, `rules/`, or >=300 total files) and posts/updates an idempotent scope advisory comment + `advisory: design-doc-suggested` label.
7. **`docs/designs/oss_pr_triage_governance.md` & `docs/designs/README.md` (New / Updated)**: Adds the approved EGM Design Document for Open-Source PR Triage & Contribution Governance and registers it in the design index.

## Human Accountability Affirmation

- [x] I am a human contributor. I have personally reviewed, understood, and can explain every line of this change in review (using AI tools to write code is welcome, but human understanding of the submitted change is required).

## Verification

- [x] **For Design Doc PRs (Stage 1)**: Executed `/egm-review docs/designs/<name>.md`, resolved findings via `/goldfish-review-resolve`, and verified relative links (`pytest tests/unit/test_link_integrity.py`).
- [x] **For Bug Fix / Implementation PRs (Stage 2)**: Unit tests or `test_scenarios.yaml` added/updated and `pytest tests/unit` executed.
